question: Does ordinary pure infiniteness imply its stronger operator-algebra version?
idea: Pure infiniteness describes a form of abundant internal duplication in a C*-algebra. The manuscript claims the ordinary and strong versions coincide. For the specified exact and nuclear algebras, further criteria imply absorption of the infinite Cuntz algebra. These structural meanings of “infinite” are more specific than simply having infinitely many elements.
why: The study of collections of transformations acting on spaces of functions. These structures appear in quantum theory and infinite-dimensional geometry.

glossary.meaning: A collection of operators with algebraic and analytic structure; these objects are important in quantum mathematics.

exactClaim: Resolves the ordinary-to-strong pure-infiniteness question of Kirchberg and Rørdam for complex C∗-algebras. For exact algebras, proper infiniteness of one fixed finite amplification of every positive element also suffices. Consequently, every separable nuclear algebra with this property absorbs $\mathcal O_\infty$, without unitality or simplicity assumptions. )
